name: From Napster to Netflix
description: How music and film went from shelves of discs and tapes to a stream on your phone: the formats, the pirates, the players and the services that changed entertainment.

checkpoints.name: Tapes and discs
checkpoints.note: The Compact Cassette and the Walkman take music outside, and the VHS tape beats Betamax in a format war. The compact disc brings clean digital sound, and LaserDisc shows a taste for sharper film at home.

checkpoints.name: Digital formats
checkpoints.note: MP3 shrinks songs to a size computers can handle, and players such as QuickTime, RealPlayer and Winamp make them playable. The DVD replaces tapes, and a revolution waits for faster connections.

checkpoints.name: The file-sharing years
checkpoints.note: Napster, Kazaa and BitTorrent let anyone share songs, and the music industry sues. Apple, led by Steve Jobs, answers with the iPod and the iTunes Store, which sell songs for a small price.

checkpoints.name: Video and streaming
checkpoints.note: YouTube, Netflix, Hulu and Spotify move entertainment from files on disks to streams, and Netflix draws customers away from rental shops such as Blockbuster. Blu-ray wins its war with HD DVD, just as discs begin to fade.

checkpoints.name: Streaming everywhere
checkpoints.note: Subscriptions replace ownership. Apple Music and Spotify fight over listeners, Twitch brings live gaming to the screen, and artists look for direct ways to reach fans.
